symbols.name: alpha
symbols.def: Hölder smoothness of the propensity score.

symbols.name: beta
symbols.def: Hölder smoothness of the arm regressions.

symbols.name: gamma
symbols.def: Hölder smoothness of the conditional effect.

symbols.name: L
symbols.def: Common Hölder radius and boundedness constant.

symbols.name: c_0
symbols.def: A sufficiently small fixed sparsity constant depending only on the class parameters.

symbols.name: O
symbols.def: One observed record \(O=(Y,A,X)\); the bounded first coordinate is the operational privacy domain.

symbols.name: sim_1
symbols.def: \(D_n\sim_1D_n'\) when the datasets differ in at most one record by replacement.

symbols.name: M_epsilon
symbols.type: Markov kernel from \(\mathcal O^n\) to an output space

symbols.name: Q_h
symbols.def: The side-\(h\) cube centered at \(x_0\), with volume \(H=h^d\).

symbols.name: k
symbols.def: Number of congruent microcubes in \(Q_h\), so \(k=H/\ell^d\).

symbols.name: C_j
symbols.def: The \(j\)-th cell of a deterministic half-open partition, \(j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\).

symbols.name: B
symbols.def: Fixed vector of scaled monomials through degree \(\lceil\gamma\rceil-1\) on \(Q_h\), with intercept first.

symbols.name: e_1
symbols.def: The first coordinate vector, selecting the intercept of \(B\).

symbols.name: M
symbols.def: \(M=\binom{d+J}{J}\), the dimension of the degree-\(J\) polynomial space on one microcell.

symbols.name: Phi_j
symbols.def: \(\Phi_j=(\phi_{j1},\ldots,\phi_{jM})\) is a fixed public basis orthonormal in \(L_2(C_j,\ell^{-d}dx)\).

symbols.name: P_hl
symbols.def: Projection onto cellwise polynomials on \(\{C_j\}_{j=1}^k\) through degree \(J\).

symbols.name: V
symbols.type: Euclidean vector with the same coordinate dimension as \(B\)

symbols.name: W
symbols.type: Square matrix with the same coordinate dimension as \(B\)

symbols.name: F_lj
symbols.def: \(F_{lj}(O)=B_l(X)A\Phi_j(X)\) for \(l\in\{1,\ldots,p\}\) and \(j\in\{1,\ldots,k\}\), interpreted as zero off \(C_j\).

symbols.name: S_hl
symbols.def: \(S_{h,\ell}=(s_1^V,\ldots,s_p^V;\operatorname{vech}_{l\le r}(s_{lr}^W);q_1^V,\ldots,q_p^V;\operatorname{vech}_{l\le r}(q_{lr}^W))\) in this exact release order.

symbols.name: Z_hl
symbols.def: A vector of mutually independent \(\operatorname{Laplace}(\Delta_1(S_{h,\ell})/\epsilon_n)\) coordinates.

symbols.name: bar_V
symbols.def: \(\bar V=\widetilde s^V-\widetilde q^V\), where tildes denote the corresponding coordinates of \(S_{h,\ell}+Z_{h,\ell}\).

symbols.name: bar_W
symbols.def: \(\bar W_{lr}=\bar W_{rl}=\widetilde s_{lr}^W-\widetilde q_{lr}^W\) for \(l\le r\), with symmetric duplication performed after the release.

symbols.name: tilde_W
symbols.def: The Frobenius projection of \(\bar W\) onto \(\{G:\lambda_-I_p\preceq G\preceq\lambda_+I_p\}\), equivalently eigenvalue clipping.

symbols.name: T_priv
symbols.def: For \(n\ge2\), \(T_{\mathrm{priv}}(h,\ell)=\operatorname{clip}_{[-2,2]}(e_1^\top\widetilde W^{-1}\bar V)\); for \(n<2\), it is zero.
symbols.role: unique total private second-order local estimator

symbols.name: zeta_h
symbols.def: A macro cutoff supported in \(Q_h\) and equal to one at \(x_0\).

symbols.name: theta_j
symbols.def: A bounded-overlap scale-\(\ell\) squared partition of unity satisfying \(\sum_j\theta_j^2=1\) near \(\operatorname{supp}(\zeta_h)\).

symbols.name: W_H
symbols.def: Minimum expected record Hamming distance over couplings of \(\Pi_+^n\) and \(\Pi_-^n\).

symbols.name: H_transfer
symbols.def: Stabilize a nonprivate nearly minimax pointwise-CATE procedure by rewriting its local score into bounded first-order and occupancy-normalized second-order blocks, then privatize one joint release and prove an oracle inequality relative to its original risk.

standard.name: Fixed interior point, specialized from Theorem 1 to a compact interior cube

novel.justification: The ordering \(\alpha+\beta<\gamma\) deliberately isolates the coupled-nuisance privacy branch. It is compatible with settings where a simple treatment-effect surface is substantially smoother than treatment selection and baseline outcome response, including the audit class \(\alpha=\beta=1/8\) and \(\gamma=1\).

assumptions.condition: \(O_1,\ldots,O_n\) are independent draws from the observed-data marginal induced by \(P\).

novel.justification: Known exact uniformity is a deliberate load-bearing restriction, directly applicable to randomized benchmark experiments whose covariate locations are generated by a public uniform randomization. A deterministic uniform grid is a useful fixed-design analogue but is not covered by the iid theorem. The restriction is strictly narrower than the unknown bounded-density random-design model in Kennedy et al. and makes both projection geometry and microcell occupancy probabilities public.

standard.name: Uniform positivity in Section 1 and Proposition S5

novel.justification: This chosen pure-central asymptotic sequence class includes constant privacy budgets and polynomially decaying budgets down to \(n^{-1}\), regimes commonly used to separate sampling and privacy effects without importing a distributed-privacy model.

definitions.name: Exact-uniform coupled-nuisance Hölder class
definitions.construction: \(\mathcal M_H=\{P:(P,Y_0,Y_1,A,X)\text{ induces records in }\mathcal O\text{ and satisfies }\text{ass:consistency},\text{ass:exchangeability},\text{ass:uniform-design},\text{ass:overlap},\text{ass:propensity-holder},\text{ass:arm-holder},\text{ass:effect-holder},\text{ass:low-nuisance}\}\), indexed by \(d,\alpha,\beta,\gamma,q,L,e_0,x_0\).

definitions.name: Pure-central-private minimax risk
definitions.construction: \(R_n^{\mathrm{DP}}=\inf_{M_{\varepsilon_n}:\,\varepsilon_n\text{-DP}}\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_H}\mathbb E_{P^{\otimes n},M_{\varepsilon_n}}|T_{\mathrm{DP}}-\tau_P(x_0)|\), where privacy uses replacement adjacency \(\sim_1\).

definitions.name: Exact-uniform local projection moments
definitions.construction: With \(\langle f,g\rangle_h=H^{-1}\int_{Q_h}fg\), define \(V_l=H^{-1}\mathbb E[\mathbf 1\{X\in Q_h\}B_l(X)AY]-\langle P_{h,\ell}(B_l\pi),P_{h,\ell}m\rangle_h\) and \(W_{lr}=H^{-1}\mathbb E[\mathbf 1\{X\in Q_h\}B_l(X)B_r(X)A]-\langle P_{h,\ell}(B_l\pi),P_{h,\ell}(B_r\pi)\rangle_h\).

definitions.name: Unique total private second-order local mechanism
definitions.construction: For \(n<2\), return zero. For \(n\ge2\) and vector cell features \(f,g\), set \(U_j(f,g)=0\) when \(N_j<2\), and otherwise set \(U_j(f,g)=\{N_j(N_j-1)\}^{-1}\sum_{i\ne i':X_i,X_{i'}\in C_j}f(O_i)^\top g(O_{i'})\). Select \((h,\ell)\) deterministically from the public parameters over a finite grid satisfying \(\ell\le h\) and \(n\ell^d\le c_0\), with a fixed tie-break. Form \(F_{lj}(O)=B_l(X)A\Phi_j(X)\), \(M_j(O)=Y\Phi_j(X)\), \(s_l^V=(nH)^{-1}\sum_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in Q_h\}B_l(X_i)A_iY_i\), \(s_{lr}^W=(nH)^{-1}\sum_i\mathbf 1\{X_i\in Q_h\}B_l(X_i)B_r(X_i)A_i\), \(q_l^V=(kp_2)^{-1}\sum_jU_j(F_{lj},M_j)\), and \(q_{lr}^W=(kp_2)^{-1}\sum_jU_j(F_{lj},F_{rj})\). Arrange the raw coordinates in the exact order \(S_{h,\ell}=(s_1^V,\ldots,s_p^V;\operatorname{vech}_{l\le r}(s_{lr}^W);q_1^V,\ldots,q_p^V;\operatorname{vech}_{l\le r}(q_{lr}^W))\), release exactly once as \(\widetilde S_{h,\ell}=S_{h,\ell}+Z_{h,\ell}\), and add mutually independent \(\operatorname{Laplace}(\Delta_1(S_{h,\ell})/\epsilon_n)\) noise to all \(p^2+3p\) coordinates. Only \(l\le r\) Gram coordinates are released. Reconstruct \(\bar V_l=\widetilde s_l^V-\widetilde q_l^V\) and \(\bar W_{lr}=\bar W_{rl}=\widetilde s_{lr}^W-\widetilde q_{lr}^W\). With \(G_B=H^{-1}\int_{Q_h}BB^\top dx\), \(\lambda_-=(1/2)e_0(1-e_0)\lambda_{\min}(G_B)\), and \(\lambda_+=2\lambda_{\max}(G_B)\), let \(\widetilde W\) be the Frobenius projection of \(\bar W\) onto \(\{G:\lambda_-I_p\preceq G\preceq\lambda_+I_p\}\), equivalently eigenvalue clipping. Return uniquely \(T_{\mathrm{priv}}(h,\ell)=\operatorname{clip}_{[-2,2]}(e_1^\top\widetilde W^{-1}\bar V)\). Counts, symmetric duplication, spectral projection, inversion, intercept extraction, final clipping, and the deterministic bandwidth choice are unreleased postprocessing.

definitions.name: Positive exact-uniform fuzzy family
definitions.construction: For \(s\in\{-1,1\}\) and \(\lambda\in\{-1,1\}^k\), use \(D_{\mathrm{fuz}}\), \(\pi_\lambda\), \(m_{s,\lambda}\), \(\tau_s\), \(\mu_{0,s,\lambda}\), and \(\mu_{1,s,\lambda}\) as declared. Under \(P_{s,\lambda}\), draw \(X\) uniformly, draw \(A\mid X\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}(\pi_\lambda(X))\), and draw a binary \(Y\mid A,X\) with the displayed arm mean, with independent potential outcomes supplying consistency.

definitions.name: Privacy phase coordinates
definitions.construction: \(q_0=d\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), \(\nu=\gamma/(2\gamma+d)\), and, when \(\epsilon_n=n^{-t}\), \(t_s=1-q/d-q/\gamma\); in this parameterization \(r_F=n^{-(2-t)/D_F}\) whenever the truncation at one is inactive.

definitions.name: Symbolic-risk privacy-transfer handle
definitions.construction: Use \(H_{\mathrm{transfer}}\): rewrite a nonprivate estimator with risk within a constant of \(R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\) into bounded local score blocks, replace every quadratic block by the exact occupancy-normalized construction in \(S_{h,\ell}\), privatize all blocks jointly, and establish an oracle inequality whose additive term is at most \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{priv}}\).

statements.statement: On the bounded observed-record domain \(\mathcal O\), consistency, armwise conditional exchangeability, and overlap imply \(\mu_a(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y_a\mid X=x]\) for \(a\in\{0,1\}\) and \(P_X\)-almost every \(x\). Hence \(\tau(x)=\mathbb E_P[Y_1-Y_0\mid X=x]\), \(m=\mu_0+\pi\tau\), \(\lvert Y_a\rvert\le1\) almost surely, \(\lvert\mu_a\rvert\le1\), \(\lvert m\rvert\le1\), and \(\lvert\tau\rvert\le2\). Operationally, the released observed-data factors obey \(\lvert B_l(X)A Y\rvert\le K_B\), \(\lVert F_{lj}(O)\rVert_2\le K_BK_\Phi\), and \(\lVert M_j(O)\rVert_2\le K_\Phi\).
statements.justification: This separates the operational privacy support restriction on observed records from its causal identification and bounded-kernel consequences.
statements.gap: Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel assume a bounded observed outcome domain for private CATE learning; the present lemma records exactly how that observed-data restriction propagates through the causal model and this query.
statements.consumer: It licenses the complete sensitivity ledger without assuming bounded unobserved potential outcomes as a primitive condition.

statements.statement: Let \(t_\gamma(x)=B(x)^\top\vartheta\) be the degree-\(\lceil\gamma\rceil-1\) Taylor polynomial of \(\tau\) at \(x_0\), and let \(r=\tau-t_\gamma\). Then \(W_{lr}=\langle B_lB_r,\pi(1-\pi)\rangle_h+\langle Q_{h,\ell}(B_l\pi),Q_{h,\ell}(B_r\pi)\rangle_h\), and \((V-W\vartheta)_l=\langle Q_{h,\ell}(B_l\pi),Q_{h,\ell}\mu_0\rangle_h+\langle B_l\pi,r\rangle_h-\langle P_{h,\ell}(B_l\pi),P_{h,\ell}(\pi r)\rangle_h\). Consequently \(\lambda_{\min}(W)\ge c>0\) and \(|e_1^\top W^{-1}V-\tau(x_0)|\le C(h^\gamma+\ell^q)\).
statements.justification: The identity converts two rough nuisance approximations into their product while preserving the smoother CATE localization bias.
statements.gap: Kennedy et al. derive a localized higher-order product bias with nuisance pilots; the exact fixed-uniform projection identity without pilots is not in their construction.
statements.consumer: It supplies the bias calculation for a single protected higher-order release rather than separately privatized nuisance fits.

statements.statement: Suppose \(n\ge2\) and \(n\ell^d\le c_0\). For every bounded pair of cell features, \(\mathbb E[U_j(f,g)]=p_2\,\mathbb E[f(O)\mid X\in C_j]^\top\mathbb E[g(O)\mid X\in C_j]\), so \(q^V\) and \(q^W\) are exactly unbiased for the two projection-product blocks in \(V\) and \(W\). If \(K_B=\max_l\lVert B_l\rVert_\infty\) and \(K_\Phi^2=\sup_{j,x\in C_j}\lVert\Phi_j(x)\rVert_2^2\), replacement changes the complete first-order block by at most \(C_1/(nH)\), where \(C_1=2pK_B+p(p+1)K_B^2\). At most two cells change, every normalized \(U_j\) is bounded, and replacement changes the complete pair block by at most \(C_2/(kp_2)\), where \(C_2=4pK_BK_\Phi^2+2p(p+1)K_B^2K_\Phi^2\). Hence \(\Delta_1(S_{h,\ell})\le C_1/(nH)+C_2/(kp_2)\le C/(n^2H\ell^d)\), using \(p_2\asymp n^2\ell^{2d}\), \(k=H/\ell^d\), and \(n\ell^d\le c_0\). Each pair coordinate has variance at most \(C/(n^2H\ell^d)\). Counts, symmetric duplication, spectral projection, inversion, intercept extraction, and final clipping are unreleased postprocessing and contribute no sensitivity.
statements.justification: This is the early kill test: it protects counts, normalization, first-order moments, and every pair correction on every bounded dataset.
statements.gap: An ordinary all-pairs statistic has sensitivity of order \(1/(nh^d\ell^d)\); Chaudhuri et al. require projection-aware stabilization, whereas the exact design makes a different normalization available here.
statements.consumer: The lemma removes occupancy logarithms and unprotected nuisance pilots from the private CATE estimator.

statements.statement: On the known exact-uniform class \(\mathcal M_H\), for \(n^{-1}\le\epsilon_n\le1\), the displayed unique joint-release mechanism admits a deterministic finite-grid choice of \((h,\ell)\), depending only on public parameters and using a fixed tie-break, for which \(T_{\mathrm{priv}}(h,\ell)\) is \(\epsilon_n\)-differentially private under replacement adjacency and \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_H}\mathbb E_P|T_{\mathrm{priv}}(h,\ell)-\tau_P(x_0)|\le C\max\{b_n,\rho_n^{\mathrm{priv}}\}\). Before optimization its risk is bounded by \(C\{h^\gamma+\ell^q+(nh^d)^{-1/2}+(n^2h^d\ell^d)^{-1/2}+(n^2\epsilon_nh^d\ell^d)^{-1}\}\). No conclusion is asserted for an unknown bounded design density or for \(\epsilon_n<n^{-1}\).
statements.justification: A total one-shot release is the constructive half of the incremental privacy frontier.
statements.gap: Niu et al. prove privacy for modular meta-learners but no Hölder minimax utility bound; Chaudhuri et al. treat generic U-statistics rather than localized causal moments.
statements.consumer: It gives private heterogeneous-effect learners a sharp benchmark in privacy-leading regimes and a fully auditable sensitivity ledger.

statements.statement: For sufficiently small fixed amplitude constants, every \(P_{s,\lambda}\) belongs to \(\mathcal M_H\), its observed cell probabilities are uniformly positive, \(\tau_s(x_0)=-4sab+O(a^3b)\), and the one-record mixtures coincide exactly: \(\mathbb E_\lambda[P_{+,\lambda}]=\mathbb E_\lambda[P_{-,\lambda}]\).
statements.justification: The legal witness must combine target separation, exact-uniform positive design, Hölder membership, and singleton cancellation.
statements.gap: Kennedy et al.'s fuzzy family uses a support geometry tailored to nonprivate Hellinger affinity; the banked private microcell witness failed CATE smoothness when \(q<\gamma\).
statements.consumer: It supplies a same-class causal hypothesis family for a privacy lower bound without support holes.

statements.statement: Conditioning on the covariates and coupling latent-sign connected components independently yields \(W_H(\Pi_+^n,\Pi_-^n)\le Cabn^2h^d\ell^d\) whenever \(n\ell^d\le c_0\). The proof must include all component sizes: singleton components have zero cost, a size-\(r\) component has total variation at most \(Cabr^2\) times the product of its spanning-tree edge probabilities, and the resulting spanning-tree sum is convergent uniformly in \(n\).
statements.justification: Expected Hamming transport, rather than one-law total variation, is the missing object needed by central-private composite testing.
statements.gap: Acharya et al. and Lalanne et al. provide general coupling-to-testing reductions but no coupling for a smooth shared-prior CATE mixture.
statements.consumer: It permits a nuisance-sensitive private converse beyond the two-point total-variation barrier.

statements.statement: On the known exact-uniform class \(\mathcal M_H\), for \(n^{-1}\le\epsilon_n\le1\), every \(\epsilon_n\)-differentially private estimator satisfies \(R_n^{\mathrm{DP}}\ge c\max\{R_n^{\mathrm{NP}},r_G,r_F\}=c\max\{R_n^{\mathrm{NP}},\rho_n^{\mathrm{priv}}\}\). The \(r_F\) branch follows by setting \(ab\asymp r_F\), \(h\asymp r_F^{1/\gamma}\), and \(\ell\asymp r_F^{1/q}\) in the component coupling before applying a central-private two-prior testing inequality.
statements.justification: The lower bound certifies that both privacy balances are intrinsic to the causal class.
statements.gap: Cai et al. establish the direct pointwise-regression privacy barrier, while no published result adds the coupled-nuisance \(n^2\epsilon_n\) branch for CATE.
statements.consumer: It prevents private CATE algorithms from being benchmarked only against ordinary private regression.

statements.statement:
On the known exact-uniform class \(\mathcal M_H\) and within \(n^{-1}\le\epsilon_n\le1\), the bounds match as \(R_n^{\mathrm{DP}}\asymp\max\{R_n^{\mathrm{NP}},ho_n^{\mathrm{priv}}\}\) whenever either \(q\ge q_0\) or \(ho_n^{\mathrm{priv}}\ge c b_n\). Under \(\epsilon_n=n^{-t}\), \(r_F=n^{-(2-t)/D_F}\) whenever the truncation at one is inactive, and the complete benchmark partition is as follows. If \(q\ge q_0\), privacy is hidden by \(b_n\) for \(0\le t\le
u\), and \(r_G\) is the leading private branch for \(t>
u\); at \(q=q_0\) and \(t=
u\), \(b_n=r_F=r_G\). If \(q<q_0\), privacy is hidden by \(b_n\) for \(0\le t\le\kappa\), \(r_F\) is the leading private branch for \(\kappa<t<t_s\), \(r_F=r_G\) at \(t=t_s=1-q/d-q/\gamma\), and \(r_G\) is the leading private branch for \(t>t_s\).
statements.justification: The explicit phase map states exactly where the new nuisance privacy price changes the attainable risk.
statements.gap: The cited CATE and private-regression papers each have elbows, but neither derives this causal nuisance-by-privacy phase diagram.
statements.consumer: It tells analysts when privacy, rather than the unresolved nonprivate exact-uniform difficulty, determines sample size.

statements.statement: If \(d=1\), \(\alpha=\beta=1/8\), \(\gamma=1\), and \(\epsilon_n=n^{-2/5}\), then \(q=1/4\), \(D_F=6\), \(\kappa=2/7\), and \(t_s=1/2\). At \(t=2/5\), \(b_n=n^{-2/7}\), \(r_F=n^{-4/15}\), and \(r_G=n^{-3/10}\), so \(r_F\) leads. The choices \(h\asymp n^{-4/15}\) and \(\ell\asymp n^{-16/15}\) give \(\Delta_1(S_{h,\ell})\asymp n^{-2}h^{-1}\ell^{-1}=n^{-2/3}\) and \(W_H(\Pi_+^n,\Pi_-^n)\lesssim abn^2h\ell\), yielding the matched scale \(R_n^{\mathrm{DP}}\asymp n^{-4/15}\).
statements.justification: This specialization exposes any missing factor of \(n\), normalization bias, or surviving singleton before the general theorem is attempted.
statements.gap: A direct \(n\epsilon_n\) nuisance balance would give the unsupported slower scale \(n^{-3/25}\); this proposition audits the \(n^{-4/15}\) scale implied by the coupled fuzzy balance.
statements.consumer: It is a reproducible audit case for sensitivity and transport calculations.

statements.statement: Can the handle \(H_{\mathrm{transfer}}\) be completed, without using a formula for \(R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\), so that for \(q<q_0\) and \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{priv}}<c b_n\) there exists one \(\epsilon_n\)-differentially private estimator satisfying \(\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_H}\mathbb E_P|T_{\mathrm{DP}}-\tau_P(x_0)|\le C\max\{R_n^{\mathrm{NP}},\rho_n^{\mathrm{priv}}\}\)?
statements.justification: This is the only remaining step from the matched privacy-leading theorem to a global incremental-price decomposition with a symbolic nonprivate benchmark.
statements.gap: Kennedy's oracle inequalities do not imply neighboring-dataset stability, and Niu et al.'s sample-splitting guarantee does not transfer arbitrary nonprivate minimax risk.
statements.consumer: A positive answer makes any future exact-uniform nonprivate improvement automatically compatible with the sharp privacy price; a negative answer identifies the necessary stability information beyond minimax risk.

sampling_model.design: Known exact-uniform covariate law \(X\sim\operatorname{Unif}([0,1]^d)\) with independent sampling and replacement adjacency; this is a deliberate design-specific restriction rather than Kennedy et al.'s unknown bounded-density random-design model.
sampling_model.units: \(n\) independent causal records \(O_i=(Y_i,A_i,X_i)\) with bounded observed outcomes \(\lvert Y_i\rvert\le1\).
sampling_model.treatment: Binary treatment with \(e_0\le\pi(X)\le1-e_0\), consistency, and armwise conditional exchangeability.
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: No data-dependent nuisance pilot is released. One ordered vector containing the first-order score and upper-triangular Gram blocks followed by their binomial-normalized pair corrections receives independent Laplace noise calibrated to its complete \(\ell_1\) replacement sensitivity.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: Theorem 1 gives the nonprivate pointwise-CATE Hölder minimax lower rate over a model with bounded covariate density, while Theorem 2 gives a matching local-polynomial R-learner under additional design and nuisance-estimation conditions.
Theorems 1--3 and Sections 3--5 give pseudo-outcome oracle inequalities and local-polynomial CATE error bounds with nuisance-product remainders.
Theorem 6 proves an \(f\)-DP composition guarantee for the sample-split multi-stage CATE meta-algorithm, without a Hölder minimax utility rate.
Algorithm 1 and Theorem 2 use local Hájek projection thresholding to obtain central-private utility bounds for bounded-kernel U-statistics.
Theorems 1 and 3 turn expected-Hamming couplings into central-private Le Cam and Assouad testing lower bounds, including shared-mixture laws in the convex hulls.
The transport characterization in the main lower-bound section bounds private testing power through an optimal-transport problem between hypothesis laws.
Theorems 2.1, 3.4, and 4.4 establish matching pointwise Besov-regression rates up to logarithmic factors under heterogeneous distributed privacy.
Sections 1.2--1.3 introduce valid instance-adaptive output perturbation by calibrating noise to a smooth upper envelope of local sensitivity.
Theorems 1 and 3 give approximate-DP output perturbation for finite and functional queries from orthogonal two-stage CATE learners, without a pure-central Hölder pointwise minimax characterization.

tldr: On the deliberately restricted class with a known exact-uniform covariate law and bounded observed outcomes, pointwise CATE is a regression-functional hybrid whose pure-central privacy cost has two distinct scales. One second-order local estimator uses a single ordered release of first-order moments and upper-triangular pair corrections with a complete all-dataset sensitivity ledger, and a positive exact-uniform fuzzy family supplies the Hamming-transport converse. The resulting incremental price is \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{priv}}=\max\{(n\epsilon_n)^{-\gamma/(\gamma+d)},(n^2\epsilon_n)^{-1/(1+d/\gamma+d/(\alpha+\beta))}\}\). This design-specific claim is not an extension to Kennedy et al.'s unknown bounded-density model. The bounds give the full decomposition whenever privacy leads or nuisance smoothness is above the nonprivate elbow; the open question is a stability transfer from the attained benchmark to the symbolic exact-uniform nonprivate minimax risk in the remaining privacy-inactive region.

project_justification.gap: Kennedy et al. establish nonprivate pointwise-CATE minimax theory under bounded-density random design and density-qualified attainability conditions, while private CATE papers establish algorithmic privacy guarantees without a pure-central Hölder pointwise minimax frontier. None determines the additional central-private price generated by the product of propensity and outcome-regression errors on a known exact-uniform causal law.
project_justification.niche: Exact uniformity is narrower than a bounded-density design and is load-bearing: it makes the local projection geometry deterministic and the probability of at least two observations in each equal-volume microcell public. The theorem applies directly to randomized benchmark studies that generate covariate locations from a public uniform law; deterministic uniform-grid studies are a fixed-design analogue, not a claim covered by the iid theorem.
project_justification.fill: A single \(p^2+3p\)-coordinate Laplace release contains the score block, the upper-triangular Gram block, and their two exact occupancy-normalized corrections; every subsequent symmetry and spectral operation is postprocessing. Boundedness is imposed only on observed outcomes, with causal and kernel bounds derived from consistency, armwise exchangeability, and overlap. A smooth positive exact-uniform fuzzy family supplies singleton cancellation and a componentwise Hamming coupling, while one open symbolic-risk transfer question remains separate from the queued nonprivate converse.

related_work: Kennedy et al. (2024), Theorem 1 and Remark 2, analyze a bounded-density random-design Hölder model; Theorem 2 and Appendix B.8 add design-estimation conditions for attainability. Their localized fuzzy hypotheses and higher-order local R-moment architecture inform this proposal, but their class is not a citation for known exact uniformity, and their lower construction does not settle the exact-uniform nonprivate risk used here. Kennedy (2023), Theorems 1--3 and Sections 3--5, gives pseudo-outcome oracle inequalities and local-polynomial error bounds, but risk control alone supplies no neighboring-record stability. Niu et al. (2022), Theorem 6, proves \(f\)-DP composition for a sample-split multi-stage CATE meta-algorithm without a Hölder minimax utility theorem. Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel (2025), page 3 and Theorems 1 and 3, assume bounded observed outcomes and develop approximate-DP orthogonal two-stage CATE releases for finite or functional queries; they do not provide a pure-central Hölder pointwise minimax rate or the \(n^2\epsilon_n\) coupled-nuisance branch. Chaudhuri et al. (2024), Algorithm 1 and Theorem 2, stabilize bounded-kernel U-statistics using local Hájek projections; the exact-uniform binomial normalization here is a causal-specific construction. Cai, Chakraborty, and Vuursteen (2024), Theorems 2.1, 3.4, and 4.4, establish pointwise Besov-regression rates under heterogeneous distributed privacy rather than one-database pure central privacy with causal nuisances. Acharya, Sun, and Zhang (2021), Theorems 1 and 3, and Lalanne, Garivier, and Gribonval (2023), the main transport reduction, supply private testing inequalities but no smooth causal shared-prior coupling. Nissim, Raskhodnikova, and Smith (2007), Sections 1.2--1.3, explain why typical occupancy cannot replace a worst-neighbor sensitivity certificate. Every comparator is used as methodological input and is downgraded to informed-by positioning.
technical_internal_limitation: The exact occupancy normalization and deterministic projection geometry require a known exact-uniform random design with equal public cell volumes. The theorem does not cover an unknown or merely bounded covariate density, and the stated iid result does not automatically cover a deterministic uniform grid. The upper theorem contains the explicit benchmark \(b_n\); replacing it by \(R_n^{\mathrm{NP}}\) below the nuisance elbow and outside privacy-leading regimes is the stated open-ended question, not an assumed consequence of generic output perturbation.
honest_scope: The causal boundedness consequence, projection identity, pair sensitivity, fuzzy membership, component transport, upper envelope, lower envelope, and phase diagram are theorem obligations on the known exact-uniform class with bounded observed outcomes. The full symbolic decomposition is settled by those obligations for \(q\ge q_0\) and whenever \(\rho_n^{\mathrm{priv}}\gtrsim b_n\). It remains open for \(q<q_0\) when privacy is inactive relative to \(b_n\). The queued exact-uniform nonprivate converse is neither cited as established nor duplicated. As a sanity reduction, fixing the nuisances removes the fuzzy branch and leaves the usual pointwise private-regression balance \(r_G\); letting privacy vanish leaves the nonprivate benchmark symbolic. Privacy sequences with \(\epsilon_n<n^{-1}\), unknown bounded-density designs, and deterministic fixed designs are outside the stated theorem; no saturation or design-transfer claim is made for those regimes.

literature_map: The selected field-level seed combines three theorem threads while imposing a narrower design than its nonprivate anchor. Kennedy et al. (2024), Theorem 1, Remark 2, Theorem 2, and Appendix B.8, analyze bounded-density random designs and provide localized higher-order and fuzzy architectures; they do not treat the known exact-uniform class as the theorem proposed here. Chaudhuri et al. (2024), Algorithm 1 and Theorem 2, show why private U-statistics require degeneracy-aware stabilization but do not exploit public binomial cell occupancy. Acharya et al. (2021), Theorems 1 and 3, and Lalanne et al. (2023), the main transport reduction, convert expected Hamming transport into private testing bounds without constructing a smooth causal shared-prior coupling. Cai et al. (2024), Theorems 2.1, 3.4, and 4.4, give pointwise private regression rates under heterogeneous distributed privacy and calibrate no causal nuisance-product branch. Niu et al. (2022), Theorem 6, and Schröder, Melnychuk, and Feuerriegel (2025), Theorems 1 and 3, provide private CATE frameworks without a pure-central Hölder pointwise minimax frontier. Kennedy (2023), Theorems 1--3 and Sections 3--5, supplies modular oracle errors without a privacy stability certificate. Nissim et al. (2007), Sections 1.2--1.3, separates global from smooth local sensitivity. The exact-uniform release and the positive fuzzy Hamming converse therefore remain the field-level target, with every named comparator treated as informing rather than as a result strictly improved in its own model.
novelty_justification: On the deliberately narrower known exact-uniform class, the field-level kernel introduces an exact binomial-normalized local pair query within one \(p^2+3p\)-coordinate release with all-dataset sensitivity \(C/(n^2h^d\ell^d)\), a positive exact-uniform fuzzy CATE family with shared-prior Hamming cost \(Cabn^2h^d\ell^d\), and the resulting privacy term \((n^2\epsilon_n)^{-1/(1+d/\gamma+d/(\alpha+\beta))}\). It does not claim to sharpen the published nonprivate rate, extend the result to bounded-density designs, or improve general private testing inequalities.

_pre_d0_cursor.topic: Revival of banked downgraded parent stat_dp_cate_minimax_v1_holder_central_dp. Determine the incremental central-private minimax price for pointwise CATE on the exact-uniform coupled-nuisance Holder class with q=alpha+beta<gamma, leaving the separate nonprivate risk R_n^NP symbolic. Prove R_n^DP equivalent to max{R_n^NP,rho_n^priv} with an explicit phase diagram, one total private higher-order local estimator with complete all-dataset sensitivity accounting, and a matching positive-design fuzzy causal converse beyond the parent's two-point-TV barrier. Independently verify the presolved candidate rho_n^priv=max{(n epsilon_n)^(-gamma/(gamma+d)),(n^2 epsilon_n)^(-1/(1+d/gamma+d/q))}; do not restore the parent's unsupported (n epsilon)^(-q/(q+d)) formula. Do not duplicate or assume queued stat_cate_uniform_sparse_component_converse, which concerns only R_n^NP. PRESOLVE EVIDENCE REQUIRING VERIFICATION: A fixed-uniform-design projection identity makes local R-moment bias the product of alpha- and beta-projection errors plus gamma-localization bias. Binomial-normalized within-cell pair averages have exact expectation and claimed replacement sensitivity C/(n^2 h^d ell^d), avoiding nuisance pilots and occupancy logarithms. A same-class smooth fuzzy family has singleton cancellation; component maximal couplings and a spanning-tree sum claim Hamming cost C ab n^2 h^d ell^d, leading with adjacent-output DP telescoping to rho_priv=max{(n epsilon)^(-gamma/(gamma+d)),(n^2 epsilon)^(-1/(1+d/gamma+d/(alpha+beta)))}. The d=1, alpha=beta=1/8, gamma=1, epsilon=n^(-2/5) specialization gives matching n^(-4/15) upper and lower scales. UNRESOLVED BOTTLENECK: Below the nuisance elbow when privacy is inactive, replace the known nonprivate upper benchmark by symbolic R_n^NP using an independently verified comparator or a new privacy-transfer lemma; the queued nonprivate result is not assumed. EARLY KILL TEST: Verify the complete d=1 pair-release sensitivity and component-Hamming calculation at h proportional to n^(-4/15), ell proportional to n^(-16/15); stop on a surviving singleton, false factorization, or normalization bias. message: Audited every assumption and comparator against its stated source, made known exact uniformity an explicit load-bearing novel restriction, moved boundedness to the observed-record privacy domain, derived its causal and query consequences, and synchronized the field-level scope without changing the estimator, converse, or corrected phase map.
